facts.statement: Only one species, V. exxoni, is known for this genus.
facts.quote: Only a single species is known, V. exxoni

facts.statement: The genus was formally described in 2016 by Filippi and colleagues.
facts.quote: formally described in 2016 by Filippi and colleagues

facts.statement: Viavenator lived in the Santonian-aged Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: lived in the Santonian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina

facts.statement: Filippi et al. classified Viavenator into the new clade Furileusauria, which also includes Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: Filippi et al. classified Viavenator to a new clade known as the Furileusauria, which includes it as well as Carnotaurus

facts.statement: Viavenator is estimated to have measured 5.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: It would have measured 5.6 m in length

facts.statement: Viavenator possessed a brain morphology and inner ear similar to the South American abelisaurid Aucasaurus.
facts.quote: Viavenator possessed a brain morphology similar to Aucasaurus, another South American abelisaurid, and had a similar inner ear

facts.statement: Compared to Majungasaurus, Viavenator relied more on quick head movements and sophisticated gaze stabilization mechanisms.
facts.quote: Compared to the Madagascan abelisaurid Majungasaurus, Viavenator was more reliant on quick movements of the head and sophisticated gaze stabilization mechanisms

facts.statement: The type and only known species, V. exxoni, was described and named in 2016 by Leonardo Sebastián Filippi, Ariel Hernán Méndez, Rubén Darío Juárez Valieri, and Alberto Carlos Garrido.
facts.quote: La especie tipo y única conocida, Viavenator exxoni, fue descrita y nombrada en 2016 por Leonardo Sebastián Filippi, Ariel Hernán Méndez, Rubén Darío Juárez Valieri y Alberto Carlos Garrido

facts.statement: The genus name derives from the Latin terms via, meaning "road", and venator, meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de los términos en latín via, "camino", y venator, "cazador"

facts.statement: The specific name honors the Exxon oil company for contributing funding to the excavations.
facts.quote: El nombre específico rinde homenaje a la compañía petrolera Exxon por contribuir con la financiación de las excavaciones

facts.statement: The holotype fossil, cataloged as MAU-Pv-LI 530, was found at the La Invernada site in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: El fósil holotipo, catalogado como MAU-Pv-LI 530, fue encontrado en el sitio La Invernada, en el noroeste de la Patagonia Argentina

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a partial skeleton including the skull.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial con el cráneo

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the caudal vertebrae and other vertebrae widen at the extreme top in lateral view to an axe-like shape.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de no solo las vértebras caudales, así como las vértebras se ensanchan en la parte superior extrema en vista lateral en forma de hacha

facts.statement: Viavenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 86 to 83 million years ago in the Santonian.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 86 a 83 millones de años durante el Santoniense

facts.statement: Viavenator is classified as a member of the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Viavenator es clasificado como miembro de la familia Abelisauridae

facts.statement: Viavenator is a member of the clade Brachyrostra and occupies a basal position within the smaller clade Furileusauria.
facts.quote: Además es un miembro del clado Brachyrostra y dentro de este, se encuentra en una posición basal de un clado más pequeño que fue nombrado por Filippi et al., Furileusauria

facts.statement: Viavenator lived from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Viavenator is a genus of carnivorous abelisaurid theropod dinosaur.
rejected.quote: Viavenator (meaning "road hunter") is a genus of carnivorous abelisaurid theropod dinosaur
